newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks fall 0.54 pct in thin week.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks fall 0.54 pct in thin week.

text.p: Shares on Cyprus's stock exchange closed 0.54 percent lower after a week which saw volumes shrink to their lowest levels this year, analysts said.

"Even though bleak volumes suggest the absence of vivid investment activity in the sense of buying interest it is also evident, since current levels are sustained, that the market is running out of sellers," said the Cyprus Investments and Securities Corporation CISCO in its weekly report.
The CSE index closed at 74.71 points on Friday, from 75.12 points last week. The Cyprus stock exchange trades in 89 securities of 43 listed companies.
Activity on the market fell to its lowest daily level of 136,800 pounds ($255,000) on the first trading day of the week.
"The market was very quiet. We are entering the traditional holiday season," said a trader.
Banking shares lost 0.48 percent, closing at 83.52 points from last week's close of 83.93. Shares in the Bank of Cyprus (Investments) dropped half a cent to 293.5.
Trading in Bank of Cyprus shares accounted for 17 percent of total volume at Friday's session.
Shares of the Cyprus Popular Bank closed Friday at 296.5, three cents lower from last week.
Part-dividend shares of the same bank were trading five cents down at 294.5.
Shares in Hellenic Bank were trading at 279.5, one cent lower from last week and Universal Bank shares were trading at 191, two cents lower from last week.

Insurance company stocks nudged up 0.13 percent to close at 57.60 points from 57.52 points last week. Universal Life Insurance company shares rose 13 cents to 468 and fully paid shares in Paneuropean closed unchanged at 98.5.
Interamerican Insurance fully paid shares were trading at 87 cents, also unchanged from last week.

Retailing chain Woolworth, which announced its intention to seek a listing on the Athens Stock Exchange this year, was trading at 65.5 cents, down one cent from last week. Woolworth shares comprised seven percent of total trading on Friday.
Associate company Cyprus Trading Corporation, which also seeks a listing on the Athens bourse, was trading at 103.5, unchanged from last week.
Shares in national carrier Cyprus Airways were trading at 34.7 cents, unchanged from last week.

The company is due to hold its annual general meeting on Saturday. The airline, which is 80 percent state-controlled, has already reported a preliminary pre-tax loss of 2.15 million pounds in 1996 after posting pre-tax profits of 5.03 million pounds in 1995.
Blue chip cement stocks Vassiliko fully paid dropped two cents to 151.5 and Cyprus Cement retreated to 229.5 from 232 last week.
Beer and wine manufacturer KEO shares closed unchanged at 103.5 ($=0.53 pound)
